title: Setting Taxi Limits & Expanding Gas Utilities
summary:
*   **Taxi Limits & Licenses:** The city capped the total number of taxicabs at 120 and approved several new driver and vehicle licenses. One driver's permit appeal was denied.
*   **New Gas Infrastructure:** Permits were issued to Texas Public Service Company to construct new gas mains across multiple city streets, detailing placement and depth requirements.
*   **Local Business & Land Use:** A homeowner secured a two-year permit for an antique shop and interior decorating business in a residential area. An alley was permanently closed in Ridgetop Annex, and a retail liquor store license was granted.
*   **Tax Record Corrections:** Property tax valuations were adjusted for a specific property from 1932 onwards, and delinquent personal property taxes for numerous individuals and businesses were cancelled after equitable payments.

Councilman Gillis offered the following resolution and moved its adoption: (RESOLUTION)
WHEREAS, in Book 2, page 211, of the Plat Records of Travis County, Texas, there appears a
map or plat of a subdivision of land known as Ridgetop Annex within the City of Austin,
Travis County, Texas; and WHEREAS, upon said map or plat there appear various streets and
alleys, one of which alleys herein referred to is fifteen feet in width and traverses a
portion of Block 7 of Ridgetop annex, and being the alley one-half block south of, and
parallel to, East 44th Street, and extending from Caswell Avenue east to an alley
extending south from East 44th Street; and WHEREAS, said alley has never been opened to
the public; and WHEREAS, the owners of all the property abutting said alley have requested
the City Council of the City of Austin to close the above described alley; and WHEREAS,
said request has been reviewed and considered by the City Council of the City of Austin;
therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF AUSTIN: THAT that alley in
Block 7 of Ridgetop Annex, one-half block south of, and parallel to, East 44th Street, and
extending from Caswell Avenue east to an alley extending south from East 44th Street, is
hereby permanently abandoned, vacated, and closed, except the City of Austin hereby
retains the right to construct, maintain, operate, and control all public utilities in,
upon, and across the above described alley.

(RESOLUTION)
WHEREAS, the property owned by A. C. King, located at 900 South 2nd Street, in the City of
Austin, was erronesously valued for the purposes of taxation by the City of Austin for the

reasonable value thereof at such times; now, therefore, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE CITY COUNCIL
OF THE CITY OF AUSTIN: THAT the valuation of the property belonging to A. C. King, located
at 900 South 2nd Street in the City of Austin, be, and the same is hereby, fixed 470

of the City of Austin is hereby ordered and directed to receive the taxes on said property
on that valuation for each of said years, now aggregating $187.09 taxes, $9.56 penalty,
and $72.02 interest, making a total of $268.67, upon receipt of which the said Tax
Assessor and Collector shall cancel all additional taxes against said property on the
records of his office.
